column7: Arrive at opening for the gatekeeper ceremony. Visitors wearing hanbok enter free.
The garden is guided-tour only and sells out. Book online a few days ahead.
People live here and visiting hours are limited. Go in the morning and keep quiet.
Free to enter, right downtown. Pair it with a tea house in nearby Insadong.
Steep near the top with fixed ropes. Bring gloves, water and good shoes.
Try bindaetteok and mayak gimbap. Some stalls prefer cash.
A neighborhood market Seoulites actually use. Walk 10 minutes to the river after.
Small cafés inside old hanok. Weekdays are far less crowded.
Permanent exhibits are free. Don't miss the Room of Quiet Contemplation.
Celadon and Joseon art next to contemporary works. Reserve a time slot online.
Free Hallyu exhibits and photo zones by Cheonggyecheon. About an hour is enough.
Beginner classes teach one chorus in about 90 minutes. Book a day ahead.
Bear statues for each group along the street. Combine with Garosu-gil.
Dance crews cover new releases most evenings. Weekends are busiest.
Outdoor stools, cheap draft beer and dried pollack. Best in warm months.
Walk the trail from Myeongdong instead of queuing for the cable car.
Fried chicken delivers to the riverside parks. Yeouido and Banpo are easiest.
Yukhoe (beef tartare) alley is on the east side. Stalls close around 10–11pm.
Rooftop bars with Namsan views and an international crowd.
Buy the stamp map at the info center. Lanes are steep, so wear sneakers.
Pick seafood on the ground floor and have it cooked upstairs for a table fee.
A seaside temple on the rocks. Arrive early to avoid tour buses.
Capsules sell out on weekends. Reserve a time slot in advance.
Old workshop buildings turned cafés, popular with locals in their 20s.
A mountain temple reachable by subway plus a short bus ride.
Drone shows run on Saturday evenings. Check the schedule before you go.
Fish cakes, hotteok and dumplings in one covered street.
About 25 minutes to the crater rim. Check sunrise time the night before.
The summit trails need online booking. Yeongsil does not and is very scenic.
Jeju's women free-divers, a UNESCO-listed tradition. Shows depend on weather.
Turquoise water and sea-view windows. Easiest with a rental car.
Heavy but important modern history. Allow about two hours.
Thick-cut Jeju black pork grilled at the table. Dip it in melchijeot sauce.
Abalone gimbap and tangerine snacks. Stalls open in the early evening.
UNESCO-listed and now free to enter. Add Seokguram Grotto if you have time.
Grassy Silla royal tombs in the middle of town. Lovely in autumn.
Hanok cafés and small shops. Try Gyeongju bread while it's warm.
Best after dark when the pavilions reflect on the pond.
A restored traditional village next to Woljeonggyo Bridge.
About 700 hanok in one area. Consider a night in a hanok guesthouse.
Bamboo grove and the royal portrait of King Taejo, founder of Joseon.
Order the brass-bowl version, the local classic.
Runs on Friday and Saturday evenings only.
Order a kettle of makgeolli and side dishes arrive with each round.
Late-1800s Japanese and Western-style buildings from when Incheon first opened to foreign trade.
Korean jajangmyeon was born here. Have a bowl, then walk the Fairy Tale Village next door.
Water taxis and a futuristic skyline. Best around sunset.
Seafood restaurants, small rides and harbor views. An easy evening near the airport.
UNESCO-listed walls about 5.7 km around. Walk a section and try traditional archery at Yeonmudae.
The king's temporary palace. Weekend martial arts shows run in front of the gate.
Small cafés and shops inside the fortress walls, popular with young locals.
Suwon is known for extra-large marinated beef ribs grilled at the table.
The pavilion and fortress walls are lit after dark. Locals picnic on the lawn.
A short ferry from Gapyeong Wharf. Famous for its tree-lined paths from Winter Sonata.
Pedal a rail bike along an old railway line through the valley. Book ahead on weekends.
Colorful theme village used as a K-drama set. Good for photos.
A large garden by day; in winter it hosts a lighting festival after dark.
Spicy stir-fried chicken cooked at your table, the region's signature dish. Add rice at the end.
Silky tofu made with seawater. Many restaurants open early for breakfast.
A wide beach next to a calm lake with a flat walking and cycling path.
Seaside cafés with ocean views. Gangneung calls itself Korea's coffee city.
Birthplace of scholar Yi I and his mother Shin Saimdang, both pictured on Korean banknotes.
The Goblin drama breakwater and, nearby at Hyangho Beach, the bus stop from a BTS album cover.
Try squid sundae and crispy dakgangjeong chicken to go.
Take the cable car to Gwongeumseong, or hike to Ulsanbawi rock (about 4 hours round trip).
At the park entrance, with a giant bronze Buddha. Pair it with the morning hike.
Founded by refugees from North Korea. Cross the harbor on the tiny hand-pulled ferry.
Sweet crispy dakgangjeong and squid sundae are the local favorites.
A beachside Ferris wheel with sea views, lit up at night.
A UNESCO-listed clan village where families still live. Cross by boat to Buyongdae cliff for the view.
A Confucian academy with a famous open pavilion facing the river and cliffs.
Short traditional mask dance shows near the village on scheduled days. Check times first.
Braised chicken with glass noodles, invented in Andong's old market. One plate feeds two or three.
Korea's longest wooden footbridge, lit up at night over the lake.
A walking route through early-1900s houses, a cathedral and the 3.1 Movement stairs.
A large temple on Palgongsan mountain with a giant stone Buddha.
A mural alley dedicated to a beloved folk singer, with live music on weekends.
Daegu's main shopping and café district, busy with students.
One of Korea's biggest night markets. Try kalguksu and grilled skewers.
Ride the cable car up for a night view over the whole city.
A cliffside hermitage facing the sea, famous for sunrise. Expect stairs.
Walk the causeway to a small island of camellia trees and sea cliffs.
Crosses the harbor over the sea. Glass-floor cabins are available.
Soy-marinated raw crab, a southern specialty. Rice in the shell is the best part.
Seaside tent bars along the harbor, made famous by the song Yeosu Night Sea.
A huge Joseon naval command hall linked to Admiral Yi Sun-sin.
A hillside village of murals overlooking the harbor.
Up Mireuksan for views over the islands of Hallyeosu Waterway.
Downhill luge carts with sea views. Fun for all ages.
Try chungmu gimbap: plain rice rolls with spicy squid and radish on the side.
Watch live League of Legends (LCK) matches in Jongno. Tickets for T1 games sell out fast, so check the schedule early.
Beginner classes for visitors teach basic kicks and board-breaking in about an hour. Book a day ahead.
Rent a Seoul public bike (Ttareungyi) with the app and ride the flat riverside paths from Yeouido.
Busan's surf beach, with beginner lessons and board rental most of the year (wetsuits in the cold months).
Walk around the 2018 Winter Olympics ice venues and the Olympic museum.
Korea's surf capital, about 40 minutes south of Sokcho. Beginner lessons run most of the year; autumn has the best waves.
Jeju has a long horse-breeding tradition; many ranches offer short beginner rides.
Walk part of a coastal route. Route 7 near Seogwipo is a favorite.
